blocks.text: 1. Layer Normalization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202418-395038720.png

Batch Normalization, the previous topic, normalizes activations across every example within a mini-batch. Layer Normalization is a genuinely different way of grouping which values get normalized together.

Instead of normalizing across the batch, it normalizes across features within a single example, not across the batch, a genuinely simple but consequential change covered in full depth throughout this topic.
2. The Key Difference From Batch Normalization

blocks.alt: The Key Difference From Batch Normalization
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202418-818829782.png

This connects back to the normalization formula, already covered in both Feature Scaling and Batch Normalization. Layer Normalization uses the exact same standardization math, just computed across a genuinely different axis.
It computes statistics across all of one example's own features, rather than across every example in a batch, exactly the distinction that gives this topic its own distinctive name and behavior.

blocks.text: 3. Why Batch Normalization Can Genuinely Struggle

blocks.alt: Why Batch Normalization Can Genuinely Struggle
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202711-982767857.png

A genuinely real limitation of Batch Normalization, already covered in its own topic, is that its statistics depend on genuinely having a large, representative batch to compute a reliable mean and variance.
Small batches, already covered in Mini-Batch Gradient Descent, produce genuinely noisy, unreliable statistics, since too few examples cannot represent the true underlying distribution well.
4. Layer Normalization's Genuinely Direct Fix
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202713-904126263.png

Layer Normalization's genuinely direct fix is that statistics come from a single example's own features, not from other examples in the batch at all, sidestepping the small-batch problem already covered in the previous section.

This makes it genuinely independent of batch size, even a batch of exactly 1 works fine, since Layer Normalization never needed a large batch's worth of examples to compute meaningful statistics in the first place.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This independence from batch size, already covered in this topic, is Layer Normalization's single most distinctive practical advantage over Batch Normalization, especially relevant for the architectures covered in the next section.

blocks.text: 5. The Connection To Sequence Data
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202713-720384913.png

This connects forward to Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers, both covered later in this course. Sequence data often has genuinely variable batch composition and length, unlike the more uniform batches typical of image tasks.

Layer Normalization's independence from batch statistics, already covered in this topic, fits this naturally, which is exactly why it became the standard normalization choice for the sequence architectures covered later in this course.
6. The Same Learnable Parameters

This connects back to gamma and beta, already covered in Batch Normalization. Layer Normalization uses the exact same two learnable parameters, applied here across the per-example feature axis instead.

These let the network genuinely learn its own preferred scale and shift, exactly as already covered there, learned through the same Backpropagation process already familiar from every other weight in the network.
7. A Genuinely Important Behavioral Consistency
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202714-882813065.png

This connects back to Batch Normalization's own training-versus-inference split, already covered in that topic. Layer Normalization behaves identically at training and inference time, a genuinely important simplification.

This holds since its statistics never depended on other examples in the batch to begin with, already covered as its direct fix earlier in this topic, so there is no running average to maintain separately at all.
8. A Genuine Limitation With Convolutional Layers

A genuinely important limitation exists too. Convolutional layers, covered later in the CNN module, have spatial structure that Layer Normalization can distort by treating spatially meaningful features as an unordered set to normalize together.

Batch Normalization, already covered in its own topic, or specialized variants often work better there instead, since they can respect that spatial structure more naturally than plain Layer Normalization.
9. Recognizing When Layer Normalization Is Genuinely The Right Choice

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Layer Normalization Is Genuinely The Right Choice
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445202715-569637989.png

Recurrent Neural Networks or Transformers, both covered later in this course, are a direct case for Layer Normalization, since its independence from batch statistics, already covered in this topic, fits these architectures naturally.

Genuinely small or variable batch sizes are another genuine case, since its per-example statistics, already covered, stay reliable regardless of batch size, unlike Batch Normalization's own genuine struggle covered earlier in this topic.

blocks.text: 10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates Layer Normalization's core computation, normalizing each example's own features independently, in direct contrast with Batch Normalization's batch-wide statistics.

code.content:
import numpy as np

def layer_norm(activations, gamma, beta, epsilon=1e-5):
    # activations shape: (batch_size, num_features), already covered as the key difference in this topic
    # unlike Batch Normalization, statistics are computed per example, across axis=1, not axis=0
    example_mean = activations.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    example_var = activations.var(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    normalized = (activations - example_mean) / np.sqrt(example_var + epsilon)
    return gamma * normalized + beta  # the same learnable parameters already covered in this topic

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
activations = rng.normal(loc=5.0, scale=2.0, size=(4, 6))  # 4 examples, 6 features each, even a batch of 1 would work
gamma = np.ones(6)
beta = np.zeros(6)

output = layer_norm(activations, gamma, beta)
print("Original per-example means:", np.round(activations.mean(axis=1), 3))
print("Normalized per-example means (should each be near 0):", np.round(output.mean(axis=1), 3))
print("Normalized per-example stds (should each be near 1):", np.round(output.std(axis=1), 3))

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows every single example's own mean and standard deviation landing near 0 and 1 respectively, independent of the other examples in the batch, exactly the behavior already covered in this topic.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Layer Normalization normalizes across features within a single example, not across the batch.
It uses the exact same standardization formula as Batch Normalization, just along a different axis.
It fixes Batch Normalization's reliance on large, representative batches for reliable statistics.
It is genuinely independent of batch size, even working correctly with a batch of exactly 1.
This independence from batch statistics fits sequence data naturally, making it standard for Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformers.
It uses the same learnable gamma and beta parameters already covered in Batch Normalization.
It behaves identically at training and inference time, unlike Batch Normalization's running-average split.
It can distort convolutional layers' spatial structure, where Batch Normalization often works better instead.
Next up: Instance Normalization, a further variant that normalizes each individual channel of each individual example separately.
